crosswalk: Seed-First AI Act (draft v2) <-> EU Artificial Intelligence Act
status: Informational mapping for policy analysis. Not legal advice. Entries with verify=true need confirmation against the Official Journal text.

relationship_vocabulary.aligned: Same objective and broadly equivalent obligation.
relationship_vocabulary.seed_first_extends: Seed-First covers the EU obligation and extends its scope.
relationship_vocabulary.partial: Overlapping but narrower or differently framed.
relationship_vocabulary.analogous: Different mechanism serving a comparable function.

entries.notes: EU prohibits manipulative or deceptive techniques and exploitation of vulnerabilities (age, disability, social or economic situation) causing significant harm.
EU prohibits social scoring leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment. Seed-First extends the prohibition explicitly to biological, genetic, ecological and carbon metrics.

EU prohibits untargeted facial-image scraping, emotion recognition in workplaces and education, and (with exceptions) real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement. Seed-First's freedom from arbitrary surveillance is broader and technology-neutral.

EU addresses exploitation of age-related vulnerabilities and requires risk-management attention to minors. Seed-First adds an express prohibition on commodifying or sexualising children and on engagement design that exploits their developmental vulnerabilities.
EU data-governance rules require training data to take account of the geographical, contextual, behavioural and functional setting of use.
entries.guardrail_component: Process obligation (not enforced at inference time)

entries.external_provision: Art. 53(1)(a) and Annex XI; Art. 40(2); Art. 95
entries.notes: EU requires documentation of known or estimated energy consumption for general-purpose AI models, standardisation work on resource performance, and voluntary codes on environmental sustainability. It sets no binding resource budgets. Seed-First Tier 1 budgets would be new.

EU human-oversight requirements (including the ability to disregard, override or interrupt the system) support 'constraint, not command' from the operator's side. Seed-First also constrains how outputs address affected persons.

entries.external_provision: (none; cf. Charter of Fundamental Rights Arts. 11-12)
entries.notes: No specific AI Act prohibition on using AI to identify or suppress non-violent dissent. Protection currently relies on fundamental-rights law.
EU data protection is individual-centred. There is no collective Indigenous data-governance or FPIC requirement.

AI regulatory sandboxes and real-world testing provide supervised pre-deployment testing. Seed-First adds a worst-case (maximin) pass criterion and consent-based pilots for high-impact structural policies.

EU requires the ability to interrupt a high-risk system via a stop procedure and gives national authorities powers over systems presenting a risk. Seed-First adds automated circuit breakers with due-process limits.
Transparency of AI interaction, right to lodge a complaint, and right to explanation of individual decisions based on high-risk systems.
Registration in the EU database for high-risk AI systems.
Automatic logging and log retention by providers and deployers. Seed-First defaults to digests rather than personal data.
The fundamental-rights impact assessment for certain deployers and corporate sustainability reporting. The IIA adds the four seed-stock pillars and is designed to integrate with both.
Serious-incident reporting; the general deadline is 15 days.
Whistleblower protection.

Fines of up to EUR 35m or 7% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices and EUR 15m or 3% for other obligations, with the lower amount for SMEs. Seed-First mirrors this structure and adds restoration orders.
Open-source exclusions and exemptions, and SME support measures.
EU excludes AI developed and put into service solely for scientific research. Seed-First keeps Tier 3 and child protections applicable even in research.
